feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 7 (16 mm, ±0.06 m, y = 0.02 m, 0.6 kg, 0.10 m track, kp 2.2, kd 0.5) gave 14 of 20 oval completions and a score of 303.8. Its slalom line loss was 0.3 and s-bend and slalom still ended off track. Iteration 8 (12 mm at the same positions) dropped oval completions to 0, so 16 mm is required. Iteration 9 (±0.07 m span, weights still about 33 times x so the outer sensors were at ±2 weights of 2) dropped oval completions to 0 and cut slalom line loss to 0.10. That means the wider span changes the signal scale and needs the weights rescaled, not just the geometry. Your Builder's ±0.06 m platform matches iteration 7 exactly, so I keep it and the controller unchanged.

Next race: if oval completions return to about 14 of 20 and slalom line loss stays near 0.3, the platform is confirmed, and the next single change is wheel_track 0.11 m for turn authority on the s-bend and slalom. If oval completions drop while line loss falls, the span or weights are the problem, so rescale the weights to about 0.86 times before any geometry change. If the robot stays on track but still never completes the s-bend or slalom, turn authority is the limit.
requested_changes: If oval completions stay at about 14 of 20 and slalom line_loss_events stay at or above about 0.25: keep the ±0.06 m, 16 mm platform and try wheel_track 0.11 m at 0.6 kg, because iteration 1 at 0.12 m gave the lowest oscillation (0.173) and no s-bend or slalom run has passed progress 0.3 yet.

If oval completions fall while line loss falls (as in iteration 9 at ±0.07 m): keep the span at ±0.06 m or, if you want the wider margin, rescale the controller weights to about 0.86 times the ±0.07 m values, because the unscaled ±0.07 m weights gave 0 of 20 oval completions.
Do not reduce sensor_size below 0.016 m again: iteration 8 at 12 mm dropped oval completions from 14 of 20 to 0 of 20 at the same positions.
